answer: Investigated the Hugging Face transformers documentation on adding new tokens to a tokenizer. Navigated to the transformers docs index (https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/index) and the Tokenizer API reference (https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main_classes/tokenizer). Key findings: (1) tokenizer.add_tokens(new_tokens, special_tokens=False) adds new regular tokens to the vocabulary — tokens are only added if not already present; accepts str, tokenizers.AddedToken, or a list, and returns the number of tokens added; (2) tokenizer.add_special_tokens(new_tokens) adds special tokens (e.g., extra [CLS]/[SEP]-style tokens); (3) AddedToken wraps a string token to customize its behavior (single-word matching, whitespace stripping, etc.); (4) after adding tokens, call model.resize_token_embeddings(len(tokenizer)) so the model's embedding matrix matches the enlarged vocabulary.
